personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A pure, deterministic engine with tests for every wave is the kind of code I can trust; still, it is a game, not something I ship to customers.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Another arcade game is exactly the fluff I already see in this tool; at least it loads only when someone opens the cabinet.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: A fourth game for people who reach LV 4 is one more reason to keep shipping through the loop.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: It follows the OMNI KART pattern step for step, so the teams see one way to add a game; the score rule that closes the farming route is the part I care about.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: A quick win for the people who play; nothing in it reaches my customers.

objection.text: I already see omni-loop as a gimmick, fluff. A fourth game is more team time on the arcade rather than the tool, and it should at least weigh nothing for the people who never play it.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Fixed sub-steps with a 60-versus-120 test, a passability check on every wave and a guard on the import graph: the spec says how it stays correct, not just what it does.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Still fluff to me, but the engine never reaches a browser that does not open the cabinet, and the guard test proves it.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Chapters, then endless mode at double: a clear goal for players, and one plan the loop can build in waves.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: The no-death-earns-a-point invariant is written as a test over every wave; that is the lesson of SUPER OMNI WORLD turned into a rule.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Small, contained and reversible by one revert; fine, though it is not a customer feature.
